reasons: Section 7.2's requirement that Customer disclose and match any more favourable competing offer before engaging another provider is a sourcing restriction binding our party; it is unbounded as to category, duration, and has no performance-based exit, so it fails the fallback (category-limited, 12 months, auto-termination on missed service levels) and sits in walk-away territory — deviation is correctly classified.

The redline removes the first-refusal gate and affirmatively preserves Customer's freedom to engage other providers, reaching the preferred position; the 0.62 changed-character ratio reflects a necessary rewrite of a one-sentence restriction rather than scope creep, and nothing adverse to Customer is introduced.

The comment is accurate (correctly notes the conflict with Section 12.3, cites the playbook position, and offers the category/12-month/performance-exit fallback) and matches the required tone and prefix.

Scope is properly bounded: the rationale expressly leaves the pricing-disclosure/MFN dimension, the Customer non-compete, and the minimum-volume commitment to their own rules, avoiding double-flagging the same commercial term under this rule.
